The product must help residents and travelers find a nearby mosque and its actual Jama’at time without implying that an estimated arrival or an unverified timetable is reliable. Local Representatives submit information; authorized Focal Persons verify it by calling the registered Imam and approve the exact submitted version.

This specification is ready for implementation planning. Release approval depends on the evidence and unresolved decisions recorded in Sections 6 and 7; the UI prototypes alone do not establish a working service.

DiscoverSalah is a community-maintained mosque and congregation discovery website for people at home and while traveling. General prayer calculations do not establish a particular mosque’s congregation time. The service therefore records mosque-specific schedules, approved changes, verification provenance and practical entrance information. A conservative arrival model considers walking or motorcycle travel, preparation and uncertainty; Whole City search supports longer Friday and Eid journeys.

The application is designed as a React web client, a Node.js/Express modular API, a background worker and MongoDB. Immutable proposals, independent approval, scoped assignments and durable review notifications protect timetable integrity. Registered Imam contact information supports remote verification and remains private. The first release is free, with maintenance responsibilities established from launch. Later funding discussions with Islamic organizations do not introduce subscriptions, donations or payroll into the present build.

This phase specifies architecture, interfaces, detailed decision rules, the 15 supplied core UI pages, correction priorities, test cases and a conditional delivery plan. Prototype inspection is complete for documentation purposes; software execution results, routing calibration and independent review require later evidence. The intended outcome is a controlled pilot whose public claims match the quality of its data and operating capacity.

Requirements take precedence over illustrative screen text. Conflicting prototype text is logged in Section 4.3 and must be corrected before acceptance. Parameters explicitly labeled proposed require Product Owner approval and field evidence. New scope must update the SRS, this specification and corresponding tests together.

DiscoverSalah is a custom browser-based information service. Anonymous visitors select an origin, prayer and date, then compare participating mosques and congregation sessions. Management users maintain those records through controlled submissions and verification. It is not a prayer-calculation authority, a transport guarantee or a mosque attendance system.

Prayer-time calculators address astronomical prayer windows; map directories address places and navigation; local notices and messaging groups communicate mosque-specific changes. DiscoverSalah combines location discovery with accountable local timetable maintenance. Its proposed distinction is the verification and publication workflow, not an unproven claim of better coverage or accuracy than other products. No institutional previous-project catalogue or comparative field study has been established for this phase; neither is presented as evidence.

Included: location selection, list/map discovery, venue details, recurring and exceptional sessions, registration, roles and assignments, draft/review/publication, durable notifications, issue reports, missing-mosque suggestions, contributor applications and moderated expiring notices. The 15 core pages are the initial design set; supporting forms and error states still require implementation design.

Excluded: subscriptions, payments, payroll, advertisements, native mobile apps, automatic Imam calling, automated religious judgments, car or bicycle reachability, OCR timetable extraction and multi-stop journey planning. English and Urdu switching is included. Automated user reminders and future-departure planning are deferred; required in-account submission and decision notifications remain included.

Begin with any willing mosque with management permission, assigned data maintenance and an independent Focal Person; do not wait for three complete areas. Keep public discovery free. Grow through Imam announcements at Friday prayer and mosque notice boards or QR links. Monitor maintenance workload and verification delays so expansion does not outpace local support. Funding discussions with Islamic organizations may follow demonstrated coverage and costs; no funding or payment to contributors is assumed.

Product Owner, engineering, testing and local operations responsibilities must be assigned before delivery dates are committed. Imam phone calls are human actions, with contact permission and concise verification notes; the system does not record calls by default. Demonstration names, counts, contacts and dates in the supplied UI are fixtures and must not be migrated into production.

The 15 October 2026 decisions in Section 7.4 select Google Maps and Routes API, bilingual launch, private contacts, controlled recovery and owner-led operations. Remaining prerequisites are listed in Section 7.3. A city outside the pilot can be selected only when coverage is explicitly available; the system must not imply nationwide completeness.

The selected design is a custom modular monolith. Online requests handle search, registration, editing and review. A small worker handles durable notifications and scheduled maintenance. Operational counts are limited reporting; no analytical warehouse is needed for the pilot.
Figure 2.1  Proposed runtime architecture retained from the Phase 2 baseline

The browser communicates with the API over HTTPS. Public reads use safe projections; management writes authenticate and authorize each request. MongoDB transactions commit domain changes, audit and outbox records together. External maps, geocoding and routes remain separate adapters. Hosting and provider selection are open procurement decisions, not deployed infrastructure.

Collect only operationally necessary account, assignment, venue, schedule, decision and audit data. Store private contacts separately from public venue fields. Avoid persistent storage of anonymous precise origins; redact location and contact data from logs. Reports and contributor applications use access-controlled records and the retention policy in Section 5.1.1.
Figure 2.2  Schedule records and relationships retained from Phase 2

A schedule version is an immutable full snapshot. A mutable ScheduleHead identifies approved and pending versions and carries a revision for optimistic concurrency. Explicit cancellations prevent fallback to recurring sessions. MongoDB references require application validation; they are not database-enforced foreign keys.
Figure 2.3  Identity, assignments and private venue contact boundary
Figure 2.4  Submission transaction and notification handoff

Submission uses an idempotency key and expected head revision. In a single transaction the service checks authority, stores the snapshot, supersedes the prior pending version where applicable, advances the head, creates the review task and writes audit/outbox records. A response lost after commit can be retried without creating another proposal. A changed payload with the same key is rejected.
Figure 2.5  Independent verification and exact-version approval

The Focal Person calls the registered Imam; a displayed phone number or ticked checkbox alone is not evidence of a completed call. Record who was contacted, when, the verified scope and outcome. Unreachable or ambiguous contact leaves the task pending or returns it for correction. Future-effective approval does not publish early.

Use React and TypeScript for the responsive browser interface, Node.js/Express with TypeScript for the API and worker, and a MongoDB replica set for transaction support. These are design selections; pin supported versions and dependencies when the repository is initialized. The supplied standalone HTML is a UI reference, not the production React implementation.

Host the website on Vercel. The Product Owner initially owns monitoring, support, backups and recovery. MongoDB remains a separate transaction-capable database; its hosting and backup mechanism still require selection. Adapt API execution to the chosen deployment and use a durable scheduled or queue-driven runner for outbox work; do not assume a permanent process inside a request function. Keep staging separate and secrets server-side. Internet access is needed for clients and chosen providers; offline editing and offline verification are not promised. Size the pilot from load measurements, not invented user forecasts.

A modular monolith reduces deployment and operational overhead compared with microservices. MongoDB fits document-shaped immutable proposals but requires deliberate indexes, transactions and integrity checks; PostgreSQL is a credible alternative with stronger relational constraints. Retain the agreed database unless an implementation review establishes a concrete benefit from changing it. A worker and outbox avoid the initial cost of a broker while preserving durable handoff.

Use Google Maps for mapping and Google Routes API with WALK and TWO_WHEELER. Validate local routes, restrictions, licensing, privacy, quotas and costs before enabling positive estimates. Do not substitute a car route and relabel it motorcycle. Until a suitable mode is validated, show the timetable and clearly unavailable arrival estimates.

Routes above are proposed Phase 3 contracts within the Phase 2 API namespace. Freeze exact request/response schemas in OpenAPI before parallel client/server development. Errors use code, safe message, field errors where relevant and requestId. Never return stack traces or private contacts in public errors.

Validate IDs, IANA timezone, calendar dates, wall-clock times, effective intervals, session uniqueness, venue ownership and explicit cancellation. The server derives actor and role from the session. Recheck account/assignment revisions and schedule head inside the write transaction. A UI-disabled button is not an authorization control.

Resolve an exact prayer/date/session before routing. Apply valid dated overrides and cancellations before recurrence. Multiple Friday sessions are separate choices; ordinary Dhuhr is not silently added unless explicitly confirmed. Eid dates may remain provisional and an outdoor venue requires its own entrance. Khutbah time is separate from congregation start.

Margin = session start − departure time − route duration − preparation allowance − uncertainty allowance. Proposed minimum preparation: 5 minutes walking, 8 minutes motorcycle, adjustable upward. Mode-specific uncertainty must be field-validated; zero is not an assumed default. Illustrative test: start 13:30, depart 13:00, route 15, preparation 5, uncertainty 5 gives +5 minutes. These fixture values are not field calibration results.

Refresh active results at least every 60 seconds and on resume using server-aligned time. Rank predictably by eligibility group, freshness, travel time, session time and stable ID. Do not claim city-wide fastest ordering from a partially routed batch. Use stable base pagination by session time and ID, and identify the subset evaluated for travel.

Nearby uses the proposed default 5 km and maximum 7 km; Whole City uses participating city membership without the 7 km cap. An origin outside that city may still be used. The city’s geographic scope does not imply every mosque has been onboarded.

Use plain labels: Walking, Motorcycle, Jama’at time, Last phone verification and Representative reconfirmation. Keep approved values distinct from pending proposals. Explain why a result is unavailable. Never use color alone for status or put private Imam contact details on public pages.

The supplied design uses Inter with 16 px body text, 24 px line height, forest green, mint surfaces and white cards. Normalize the production tokens against the earlier design brief before implementation: primary #146B4A, background #F7FAF8, text #172B23, secondary #52635B, warning #8A4B08 and error #B42318. Screens in this document retain the supplied palette. Target 48 px controls, visible keyboard focus, meaningful labels, logical headings, 200% zoom and mobile reflow. Contrast and assistive-technology behavior must be tested; conformance is not yet established.

The public flow must work without an account. Invite-only management sign-in resolves permissions from the server. A contributor application is a request for consideration, not self-assignment. Add confirmation only for consequential actions such as approval, reassignment and revocation, and preserve entered data when validation fails.

Use Google Maps and Google Routes API for distinct walking and motorcycle modes. Confirm the real entrance pin during onboarding. Never relabel car or bicycle routing as motorcycle. Show Estimated reachable, Time is tight or Arrival estimate unavailable with reasons and assumptions; no arrival or attendance guarantee.

Google documents walking and two-wheeler routes as beta and requires a warning about potentially incomplete paths. Display the applicable provider warning and attribution where routes are shown. Motorcycle calls have higher billing rates. Keep restricted routing credentials on the server and apply provider quotas, application request limits and billing alerts; alerts alone do not enforce a spending cap.

Route a bounded, visibly identified subset of eligible results. Whole City still lists participating matches through stable pagination, including unrouted results labeled not evaluated. Do not equate unevaluated results with unreachable results or claim the fastest result across a partially evaluated city. On provider failure or usage-limit exhaustion retain timetable and map/list discovery with arrival unavailable.

Field-test walking and motorcycle allowances separately before enabling positive estimates. Preserve the preparation and uncertainty model in Section 3.1.1. Navigation opens only on explicit user action and uses the verified entrance; disclose the handoff to the external provider.

Provide a visible language switch on public and management pages. Persist the preference locally; keep the current page, selected prayer/date, origin, filters and unsaved form content. Translate labels, errors, status explanations and core help; do not automatically translate names or alter entered timetable values.

Use Urdu right-to-left layout and an Urdu-capable font. Keep phone numbers, email addresses, URLs and numeric time fields isolated in the correct direction. Test mixed-language content, mobile reflow, keyboard navigation and all 15 core pages in both languages. The supplied screenshots remain English prototype references; Urdu layouts require implementation and acceptance testing.

These are inspection findings in the supplied HTML. They are open design/implementation tasks, not independently validated software defects. Do not adopt the conflicting text as a new requirement.

Use these as focused forms, tabs or states where practical. The 15 main page designs remain the initial navigation set; they do not remove the supporting requirements from the release backlog. If capacity requires deferring a workflow, record the scope decision rather than marking it complete.

Rendered crops preserve supplied UI content and demonstrate selected task regions. The local supplied logo is used where the remote logo asset fails; fonts and icons are loaded for readable rendering. Illustration photos and map placeholders are not field evidence. The figures do not certify responsiveness or functional navigation. Do not store example personal details as production records.

Use opaque server sessions in Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies with CSRF protection and origin checks for state-changing requests. Rate-limit authentication and public submissions; use safe generic login errors. Admin access requires MFA. Authorization evaluates role, active account, scope, assignment revision and no-self-approval on the server. Recovery and retention follow Section 5.1.1. Session and invitation expiry settings must be configured and tested before launch.

Allowlist public fields rather than deleting known private fields after serialization. Keep registered Imam numbers and verification notes available only to authorized management. Avoid logging passwords, tokens, precise origins and full phone numbers. Limit contact collection to purpose and permission; do not collect CNIC by default. Restrict audit access and make app-level history append-only.

Visitors can browse, search and navigate without signing in. Request location only when needed and offer manual entry. Use precise origin coordinates transiently for the query; do not create a location-history record or include coordinates in application logs. Explain the transfer to Google when requesting routes; provider processing is separate from our retention policy.

Store the Imam verification number privately with permission to contact. Permit access only to assigned personnel who need it and authorized administration. A public mosque office contact is a separate optional field with explicit publication permission. Changing private contact details requires independent evidence; a new number cannot verify itself.

Management accounts are individual and invitation-only. Use verified email for password recovery. Reset tokens are securely generated, stored hashed, single-use and expire after 15 minutes. Rate-limit requests and use the same response for known and unknown emails. On successful reset, invalidate existing sessions and notify the account holder. Do not automatically log the user in.

If email access is lost, the Product Owner checks identity through an existing trusted mosque contact before changing recovery details. Record the evidence and decision; a newly supplied number alone is insufficient. Require admin MFA and offline recovery codes. Never transmit shared or replacement passwords to staff.

Retention deletion is an authorized, auditable process distinct from routine append-only history. Preserve minimal deletion markers long enough to prevent backup restoration from reintroducing deleted data. These are accepted operational defaults, not a claim of statutory retention requirements.

Approval commits independently of notification delivery. The worker retries with leases, bounded backoff and deduplication; repeated failure raises an operational alert. A delayed activation worker cannot expose future timings early because reads check effective instants. A revoked or missing maintenance assignment makes the affected scope maintenance-pending and blocks positive arrival claims until coverage is restored.

Proposed operational targets are 99.5% availability, daily backups, RPO 24 hours and RTO 4 hours. Daily encrypted backups and a 30-day rolling backup retention are accepted. Availability, RPO and RTO remain planning targets until the separate database setup and restore rehearsal establish feasibility. Monitor API errors, route timeouts, oldest review age, stale coverage, outbox failures and assignment gaps; route initial alerts to the Product Owner and document a trusted emergency handover path before pilot.

Proposed reconfirmation/freshness thresholds of 7 and 14 days and final event verification within 48 hours require owner approval. Store separate timestamps for representative reconfirmation and independent phone verification. A changed proposal or dispute affects its exact prayer/date scope, not every unaffected session. Expired or provisional event information must not remain positively ranked.

Moderated notices cover religious events, service information and death/Janazah announcements with source authority and consent appropriate to the content. Publish minimal necessary information, provide correction/cancellation and enforce expiry on reads. Janazah route feasibility is deferred unless separately specified. The team visits mosques to obtain permission and verify initial listings. After activation, use a management-approved poster with a website link and mosque-specific QR code, and Imam announcements. Social posts invite Focal applicants; review and scoped invitation precede access. No paid placement changes ranking.

Testing begins with pure schedule and arrival rules, then API integration against a transaction-capable database, UI journeys and recovery/security checks. Provider contract tests use deterministic stubs; field journeys validate actual route uncertainty separately. No stub result establishes real-world route accuracy.

Entry requires a versioned build, approved test configuration, isolated staging, transaction-enabled database, synthetic accounts/venues and controlled provider responses. Record commit/build ID, environment, parameters, tester, execution time, evidence path and actual results for every run. Do not use real Imam phone numbers in automated fixtures.

No application test executions have been evidenced for this phase. Zero runs below is a coverage status, not proof of quality. Defect counts from unexecuted testing are unknown. The prototype findings are tracked separately to avoid presenting a static inspection as software validation.

High covers timing trust, authorization, privacy or arrival claims that can materially mislead users. Medium covers impaired workflow, accessibility and consistency. Engineering owns correction; QA verifies the same build with regression evidence; the Product Owner accepts remaining lower-risk limitations. Record ID, severity, affected version, reproduction, expected/actual result, owner, status, evidence and verified fix build.

A critical or High unresolved issue in timing integrity, unauthorized access or private-data exposure blocks pilot release. Disabling an affected feature is acceptable only when the remaining experience is truthful and the Product Owner records the reduced scope. Passing tests does not establish universal prayer attendance or route guarantees.

For each executed case append build ID, environment, configuration version, tester, timestamp, actual result, status and evidence reference. Link any defect and rerun evidence. Retain provider-stub results separately from field observations. Record blocked tests and their dependencies rather than marking them passed by review.

The plan below retains eight candidate two-week sprint buckets from the Phase 2 planning baseline. They are sequencing estimates, not committed calendar dates. Team size, working hours and remaining supporting scope must be estimated before dates are promised. Testing occurs throughout, not only in the last sprint.
The editable Word matrix is a relative Gantt chart. Filled cells indicate planned work windows; no cells imply completed implementation. Dependencies take precedence over overlapping cells.

Track delivery by completed acceptance evidence and a working increment. Do not report sprint velocity, completion percentage or defect-removal time until measured. If route validation or staffing slips, offer truthful timetable-only coverage or delay the affected area; do not relax verification to meet a date.

Version 1.1 records the Product Owner’s instructions and acceptance on 15 October 2026. These changes supersede conflicting pilot, language, provider and privacy assumptions in earlier documents. Synchronize the SRS and SDS during the next documentation update; this edition does not claim those files have already been revised.

Freshness thresholds remain provisional as explicitly stated in the preceding discussion. No approval of a maps provider constitutes proof of local routing accuracy. Database hosting, budget amounts and staffing names remain implementation prerequisites, not invented commitments.

Community managed mosque discovery and practical Jama’at planning

DiscoverSalah is a real-world public service that helps people discover mosque-specific congregation timings and assess whether they can arrive in time. It supports walking and motorcycle travel, nearby discovery, and whole-city planning for daily prayers, Jumu’ah and Eid. Its value depends on trustworthy schedules and realistic travel estimates, supported by accountable local people.

This proposal updates Version 3.0 and removes the academic-project framing. It establishes product scope and operating rules for implementation planning. The formal requirements document, detailed acceptance criteria and technical specifications will follow the templates supplied by the project owner.

Motorcycle travel is included from the first release alongside walking. Local Representatives submit mosque information and timing changes; their Focal Person receives an account notification and can verify timings by calling the Imam whose number was collected during registration. Physical visits are not a prerequisite. A Whole City search mode removes the nearby distance cap for discovery, including Friday and Eid congregations.

The remaining workflow details in this proposal are recommendations, rather than previously approved requirements. In particular, timing publication after phone verification, freshness thresholds, review targets and launch metrics are proposed defaults to confirm through operating experience and the forthcoming requirements process.

People should be able to find the correct prayer or event, see confirmed mosque timings, compare practical travel options, and open directions. Representatives should be able to submit updates quickly. Focal Persons should be able to verify changes remotely and identify overdue work. Administrators should be able to expand coverage without losing responsibility for data quality.

Begin with a controlled operational launch in one selected city and a manageable network of participating mosques. Both Nearby and Whole City modes are available immediately. City-wide discovery means searching all participating venues in that city; it does not imply every mosque has already been onboarded.

Users choose their starting location, travel mode, prayer or event, and search scope. Location permission is optional: manual area selection and a movable starting-point pin remain available. Browsing does not require an account. A confirmed origin is needed for personalized travel estimates; users can still browse timings without it.

Each card shows the mosque or event venue, neighborhood, prayer name, congregation start, date, timing confirmation status, estimated journey duration, arrival margin and directions. Khutbah or arrival-advice times are separate from the congregation start. Available facilities and access restrictions are shown when confirmed; unknown facilities are not assumed.

If today’s selected Asr sessions have all started, show “No upcoming Asr Jama’at found today.” Do not silently switch to Maghrib. In the general discovery mode, tomorrow’s Fajr can appear after Isha with an explicit Tomorrow label and a valid schedule.

Support multiple Jumu’ah sessions and dated Eid sessions at mosques or authorized associated prayer grounds. Every session has a responsible representative and verification history. Outdoor venues require their own entrance coordinates, location description and access information. Eid dates may remain provisional until locally confirmed; provisional sessions are visible for planning but cannot receive positive reachability recommendations.

Whole City is a separate search scope, not a larger circle around the user. An origin outside the selected city can still be used for travel estimation. Adjacent cities require an explicit city change. Clearly display coverage limitations and never imply that no search result means no congregation exists.

Bike means motorcycle in this proposal. Users explicitly choose Walking or Motorcycle; changing the mode recalculates journey time and rankings. The production design uses route-based estimates appropriate to the mode, with routing coverage and motorcycle restrictions tested in the launch city before release. A car estimate must not be labeled as a motorcycle estimate.

Routing-provider selection remains open. Evaluate local walking and motorcycle coverage, route legality, response time, usage costs, privacy and licensing. If reliable motorcycle routing is unavailable, use a separately validated local model only with explicit estimate labeling. Where neither method is credible, display “Travel estimate unavailable” and withhold a positive reachability label. Straight-line distance alone is not the default basis for city-wide recommendations.

Arrival margin = congregation start − departure time − estimated route duration − preparation buffer − uncertainty allowance. For immediate discovery, departure time is server-aligned current time. For future planning, the user supplies a departure time and the result is labeled a forecast that must be refreshed before leaving.

The preparation buffer covers parking, walking from the entrance and Wudu. A proposed starting minimum is 5 minutes for walking and 8 minutes for motorcycle travel; users may increase it. Friday and Eid can need longer venue-specific buffers. Additional uncertainty depends on measured route errors and available traffic information. These values require local calibration and are not guarantees.

Filter by prayer, date, scope and publication status first. Group results by reachability, then prioritize stronger timing confirmation, shorter mode-specific travel duration, earlier session time and a stable identifier. Offer explicit Earliest Jama’at and Shortest Journey sorting. Distant sessions remain discoverable in Whole City mode; pagination and routing batches must not silently restrict the search to nearby mosques.

Example: at 12:30 PM, a confirmed 1:00 PM session has a 15-minute motorcycle route, 8-minute preparation buffer and 5-minute uncertainty allowance. The arrival margin is 2 minutes: estimated reachable. A 12:55 PM session with identical assumptions is too tight. Both are illustrative, not measured journeys.

The System Admin creates Focal Persons and assigns their geographical responsibility. Focal Persons create Local Representative accounts and assign mosques. Representatives maintain only assigned records. Public users can discover and report information but cannot publish official changes. Account privileges are enforced by the backend on every protected operation.

The representative enters the mosque name, address, map pin and entrance, city and area, initial timetable, Imam’s name and phone number, and relevant facilities. Record permission to use the Imam’s number for service verification. Check possible duplicates by location and identity before publication. Supporting timetable photographs may be included but do not replace the defined verification decision.

Submitting registration creates a notification and review task in the assigned Focal Person’s account. The Focal Person calls the registered Imam to confirm mosque identity, the representative’s relationship, and the timetable, then records the call outcome and approves or returns the submission. No physical visit is required. If the Imam cannot be reached, the submission stays pending and can be escalated; it is not marked verified.

DiscoverSalah addresses the difficulty of finding current mosque-specific congregation times and judging whether a journey can finish before prayer begins. It combines maintained mosque records, dated sessions, geospatial discovery, route estimates and transparent timing status. Public users search without an account, select walking or motorcycle travel, and choose nearby or whole-city discovery. Friday and Eid planning supports multiple sessions and distant venues.

The management model links each mosque to a Local Representative and a supervising Focal Person. Representatives submit information; Focal Persons receive account notifications and verify it by calling the registered Imam. The proposed publication policy protects unverified changes while preserving an audit trail. The intended result is a usable and accountable public service, to be validated through actual journeys and mosque operations. No market-size, adoption or field-accuracy claim is made here.

Product goal: enable people to find a relevant, maintained congregation and understand the estimated time needed to reach it. Current pain points described in the proposal are scattered timings, local changes, unfamiliar locations and no clear maintenance responsibility. These are project hypotheses pending user research, not findings from a completed survey.

Target users include local worshippers, commuters and travelers who do not know the nearest participating mosque or its Jama’at time. Discovery uses their current or chosen location. The service supports walking and motorcycle journeys, including longer Friday and Eid trips; it does not promise arrival or search along an entire travel itinerary.

Preconditions: valid origin, mode, selected session and current route estimate. UC-15 Cancel or change an event session

Preconditions: representative has authority over the event venue. Main flow: submit affected session/date and change reason; notify reviewer; immediately flag an affected confirmed session as under review; verify by phone; approve cancellation or revision. Alternatives: provisional Eid date remains provisional; reviewer unavailable invokes backup. Postcondition: cancellation is an explicit exclusion; recurring fallback cannot resurrect the canceled session.

A telephone call is a manual activity; the platform records its outcome, not proof of a completed telecom connection. Reviewers must not self-approve their own submissions. If the same person would occupy conflicting roles, route the review to an authorized independent backup or Admin. Approval after a session has started updates history but cannot restore it to upcoming results.

Margin = session start − departure time − route duration − preparation buffer − uncertainty allowance. For eligible inputs, margin ≥0 means Estimated reachable. If margin <0 but departure plus route duration is before the start, label Too tight. Arrival at or after the start means Unlikely to reach. BR-07 ineligibility takes precedence and means Reachability unavailable. Use server-aligned current time for leaving now, or the selected future departure for a qualified forecast. Calculate before rounding display values.

Submission states: Draft → Submitted → Approved, Returned or Rejected; a newer submission may mark an older pending version Superseded. Approved future schedules wait until their effective time. Listing states are separate: Draft, Published, Suspended or Maintenance pending. Notification Read is separate from review Resolved. These distinctions prevent status changes from falsely implying verification.

Public APIs return published public fields only; management APIs authorize role and record scope server-side. Invalid inputs return field-specific errors without internal secrets. Concurrent edits return a conflict with a reload path. Retried mutation requests must not create duplicate sessions or decisions. Final endpoint names and schemas belong in the design phase.

Location coordinates use a documented longitude/latitude order. Schedule interpretation uses Asia/Karachi; audit timestamps use UTC. The frontend refreshes when returning from background and at least every 60 seconds while active; server time anchors countdowns. Offline state stops live reachability claims.

Separate adapters cover geocoding, map tiles, walking/motorcycle routing and navigation handoff. Evaluate provider coverage, licensing, quotas, traffic and future-departure support before selection [R4–R5]. Future estimates lacking predictive traffic must say so. Route timeout is proposed at 8 seconds, after which results degrade to timetable-only. No paid provider or tariff is assumed.

Proposed stack remains React, Node.js/Express and MongoDB with geospatial indexing [R4]. The technology choice does not guarantee performance. City search must preserve pagination over all matching venues; progressive route loading must not pretend to be a globally complete travel-time ranking. Operational phone calls and mosque decisions remain outside the software boundary.
